bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Srini Pallia is measured and consistent — frames AI as a *structural, market-expanding* opportunity ("we have pivoted to AI") while candidly owning the soft quarter, the BFSI QoQ dip (large-deal ramp + slow discretionary), and the Healthcare/US pressure. Disciplined on guidance (one-quarter view only; won't time the margin recovery or forecast sector turns). CFO Aparna Iyer precise on the margin bridge and deal-margin nuance (accretive "Reimagine AI" vs give-backs on cost-take-out deals), and firm on non-disclosure (won't split organic/inorganic guidance). Balanced tone — invests for the future without over-promising the timeline.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Guidance is only one quarter out, and it's negative-to-flat** — the demand trough isn't called; H2 hinges on slipped large deals converting and EMR/BFSI-Americas ramps.
- **Ex-Mindsprint, headcount fell 2,500 QoQ** — the reported headcount rise is entirely the acquisition; underlying is still shrinking, consistent with AI-productivity + soft demand.
- **AI is both the risk and the pitch** — mgmt concedes SDLC productivity compresses the traditional book, but argues the offset is "Reimagine AI" (advisory, data priming, agent orchestration, Sovereign AI, AI-DC) at premium realizations; the mix shift is the whole equity story.
- **Margin-band recovery deliberately un-timed** — 16% → 17–17.5% is a "mission," not a dated commitment; levers (pyramid/agentification, bench, G&A) exist but revenue softness gates the pace.
- **Ecosystem breadth is a signal** — CoEs/awards across **both Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI**, plus Wipro Ventures into AI startups, position Wipro as model-agnostic in the "platform + service" future it describes.

latest_quarter.body: Margin fell 120 bps YoY to 16% on: (1) incremental salary-increase (MSI) impact, (2) AI + deal investments, (3) newly-closed acquisitions entering execution — partly offset by INR depreciation + operational efficiencies. Levers to reclaim 17–17.5%: automation/AI/productivity (FPP), G&A, higher bench utilization, pyramid restructuring / "agentifying" existing programs. Deal-margin math is deal-specific: cost-take-out/large traditional deals carry forward-productivity give-backs and competitive pressure; "Reimagine AI" / data / advisory / smaller data-modernization work is rate-accretive and net-positive to realizations. outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: As an asset-light IT services business, Wipro's 'expansion' is footprint, platform and ecosystem build-out rather than physical capacity. It operates 10 innovation/Wipro Innovation Network labs across 10 global locations as of May 2026 (United States, United Kingdom, Australia, UAE, South Korea, and India). Wipro Ventures, its corporate investment arm, has a $500 million fund to invest in early-to-mid-stage enterprise software startups (GenAI/AI, Cybersecurity and Data Security, App Modernization, Data Analytics, DevOps/Test Automation, Vertical SaaS), with 40+ total investments, 25+ companies in the active portfolio, 750+ startup solutions, 280+ global clients over 10 years, and 16 successful portfolio exits. Platform/talent build-out includes Topcoder (an open innovation/crowdsourced talent platform with a global community of over two million developers) and research collaborations with IISc Bengaluru, MIT, and IIT Delhi. During the year the company expanded its AI ecosystem partnerships, including large-scale deployment of Microsoft Copilot Studio, a global collaborative agreement with Factory.ai for agent-native software engineering, an expanded strategic alliance with ServiceNow to embed agentic AI workflows across IT services, HR, procurement and cybersecurity operations, and a strengthened collaboration with OpenAI for AI-led transformation in financial services and energy.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- IT Services segment result margin improved (17.07% to 17.22% of revenue) helped by lower selling & marketing expense ratio, partly offset by higher employee compensation, sub-contracting costs to fill vacant positions, and software license costs from new technology implementation
- IT Products segment revenue growth driven primarily by acquisitions completed during the year and higher revenue from a few select customers in India
- General and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue rose partly due to the new labor code implementation in India and higher lifetime expected credit loss provisions, partially offset by lower staff recruitment expense and lower average headcount from cost optimization initiatives
- Segment mix shift across Strategic Market Units: Americas 2 revenue share and segment-result contribution rose while Europe's share of revenue and results declined slightly year-on-year
- Sector mix: BFSI remains the largest revenue sector (~34%) with Consumer, Health, Energy/Manufacturing and Resources, and Technology and Communications making up the balance; Technology and Communications share rose while Consumer share declined
- Client concentration: largest client's share of IT Services revenue and top-5 client share both rose year-on-year, indicating increasing reliance on a few large accounts even as the company seeks broader client mining

Management frames AI as market-*expanding*, funds the investment through disciplined margin levers, and targets a return to the **17–17.5%** band (no timeframe) while returning **>$3bn to shareholders** over the trailing year.

margins & cost dynamics: Margin fell 120 bps YoY to 16% on: (1) incremental salary-increase (MSI) impact, (2) AI + deal investments, (3) newly-closed acquisitions entering execution — partly offset by INR depreciation + operational efficiencies. Levers to reclaim 17–17.5%: automation/AI/productivity (FPP), G&A, higher bench utilization, pyramid restructuring / "agentifying" existing programs. Deal-margin math is deal-specific: cost-take-out/large traditional deals carry forward-productivity give-backs and competitive pressure; "Reimagine AI" / data / advisory / smaller data-modernization work is rate-accretive and net-positive to realizations. Token economics rising — clients focused on total cost of ownership / ROI (high-end LLM vs open-source), a pricing conversation Wipro leans into via its deep-tech positioning.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light services + acquisition-led. Mindsprint closed and integrating (full revenue in Q2). Investment concentrated in AI-native platforms, talent and ecosystem/Ventures. **Watch slippage:** the $1.6bn large-deal bookings (down YoY) and deals that slid to Q2 — ramp timing is the swing factor for H2; margin-band recovery timeline deliberately un-committed.
capital allocation:
- **Interim dividend Rs 2/share**; **>$3bn returned to shareholders over the trailing year** (dividends + prior buyback).
- Acquisitions (Mindsprint) + Wipro Ventures ($0.5bn) into AI/data/security startups.
- Disciplined margin focus alongside continued "invest for the future" (AI-native talent/infra).
risks & watch-items:
- **Weak Q2 guide (−1.5% to +0.5% CC)** and soft demand / longer decision cycles — growth trough not clearly called.
- **Americas softness** (Americas-2 −7.3% YoY) and **Health + EMR declines** — the sector drags.
- **Large-deal TCV down YoY** with decisions slipping — conversion risk.
- **AI cannibalization of the existing book** — SDLC productivity compresses traditional IT/BPO budgets; mgmt argues net-positive via new AI services + "human + AI always," but the transition is a revenue/margin risk.
- **Margin recovery un-timed** amid competitive large-deal pricing + AI-investment drag + token-cost/ToC pressure.
- Integration execution on Mindsprint + acquisition margin drag.
management quality / tone: Srini Pallia is measured and consistent — frames AI as a *structural, market-expanding* opportunity ("we have pivoted to AI") while candidly owning the soft quarter, the BFSI QoQ dip (large-deal ramp + slow discretionary), and the Healthcare/US pressure. Disciplined on guidance (one-quarter view only; won't time the margin recovery or forecast sector turns). CFO Aparna Iyer precise on the margin bridge and deal-margin nuance (accretive "Reimagine AI" vs give-backs on cost-take-out deals), and firm on non-disclosure (won't split organic/inorganic guidance). Balanced tone — invests for the future without over-promising the timeline.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Guidance is only one quarter out, and it's negative-to-flat** — the demand trough isn't called; H2 hinges on slipped large deals converting and EMR/BFSI-Americas ramps.
- **Ex-Mindsprint, headcount fell 2,500 QoQ** — the reported headcount rise is entirely the acquisition; underlying is still shrinking, consistent with AI-productivity + soft demand.
- **AI is both the risk and the pitch** — mgmt concedes SDLC productivity compresses the traditional book, but argues the offset is "Reimagine AI" (advisory, data priming, agent orchestration, Sovereign AI, AI-DC) at premium realizations; the mix shift is the whole equity story.
- **Margin-band recovery deliberately un-timed** — 16% → 17–17.5% is a "mission," not a dated commitment; levers (pyramid/agentification, bench, G&A) exist but revenue softness gates the pace.
- **Ecosystem breadth is a signal** — CoEs/awards across **both Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI**, plus Wipro Ventures into AI startups, position Wipro as model-agnostic in the "platform + service" future it describes.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin fell 120 bps YoY to 16% on: (1) incremental salary-increase (MSI) impact, (2) AI + deal investments, (3) newly-closed acquisitions entering execution — partly offset by INR depreciation + operational efficiencies. Levers to reclaim 17–17.5%: automation/AI/productivity (FPP), G&A, higher bench utilization, pyramid restructuring / "agentifying" existing programs. Deal-margin math is deal-specific: cost-take-out/large traditional deals carry forward-productivity give-backs and competitive pressure; "Reimagine AI" / data / advisory / smaller data-modernization work is rate-accretive and net-positive to realizations. Token economics rising — clients focused on total cost of ownership / ROI (high-end LLM vs open-source), a pricing conversation Wipro leans into via its deep-tech positioning.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As an asset-light IT services business, Wipro's 'expansion' is footprint, platform and ecosystem build-out rather than physical capacity. It operates 10 innovation/Wipro Innovation Network labs across 10 global locations as of May 2026 (United States, United Kingdom, Australia, UAE, South Korea, and India). Wipro Ventures, its corporate investment arm, has a $500 million fund to invest in early-to-mid-stage enterprise software startups (GenAI/AI, Cybersecurity and Data Security, App Modernization, Data Analytics, DevOps/Test Automation, Vertical SaaS), with 40+ total investments, 25+ companies in the active portfolio, 750+ startup solutions, 280+ global clients over 10 years, and 16 successful portfolio exits. Platform/talent build-out includes Topcoder (an open innovation/crowdsourced talent platform with a global community of over two million developers) and research collaborations with IISc Bengaluru, MIT, and IIT Delhi. During the year the company expanded its AI ecosystem partnerships, including large-scale deployment of Microsoft Copilot Studio, a global collaborative agreement with Factory.ai for agent-native software engineering, an expanded strategic alliance with ServiceNow to embed agentic AI workflows across IT services, HR, procurement and cybersecurity operations, and a strengthened collaboration with OpenAI for AI-led transformation in financial services and energy.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone

Disciplined on guidance (one-quarter view only; won't time the margin recovery or forecast sector turns). CFO Aparna Iyer precise on the margin bridge and deal-margin nuance (accretive "Reimagine AI" vs give-backs on cost-take-out deals), and firm on non-disclosure (won't split organic/inorganic guidance). Balanced tone — invests for the future without over-promising the timeline.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Consulting-led approach that starts with client business context before technology decisions, differentiating from pure delivery-led competitors
- Wipro Intelligence, a unified suite of AI-powered platforms and solutions (including WINGS and WEGA) underpinning delivery across the portfolio
- Deep industry focus across priority sectors (BFSI, Consumer, Health, Energy/Manufacturing and Resources, Technology and Communications) combined with functional depth (AI advisory, supply chain, finance transformation, people and change, sales/marketing/CX, sustainability)
- Broad global delivery scale: 240,000+ employees and business partners across 65 countries
- Strong enterprise software partner ecosystem (SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, MS Dynamics) and hyperscaler ecosystem for cloud journeys

- Specialized units (Capco, Aggne, Designit) extending domain depth in banking/capital markets/insurance and design

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
